article_title: Knee flexion of saxophone players anticipates tonal context of music
citation: Moura, N., Vidal, M., Aguilera, A. M., Vilas-Boas, J. P., Serra, S. & Leman, M. (2023). Knee flexion of saxophone players anticipates tonal context of music. npj Science of Learning 8:22. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-023-00172-z
title: R-package for computational modeling of the auditory periphery (ANI, pitch expectation, rhythmical density)
description: The authors released "the routines for the computational modeling of the auditory periphery ... freely available as an R-package at a Github repository". It computes the auditory nerve image with CalcANI, periodicity pitch images with PeriodicityPitch, pitch expectation profiles with ContextualityIndex (Comparison), and rhythmical density with RoughnessFFT. The package implements the model used to derive pitch expectation and rhythmical density profiles from audio in this study.
requirements: Mono audio recordings of the performance, converted into a 40-channel auditory nerve image.
target_learning_goals: analyzing sensorimotor coupling in performance data
key_sources: Moura, N., Vidal, M., Aguilera, A. M., Vilas-Boas, J. P., Serra, S. & Leman, M. (2023). Knee flexion of saxophone players anticipates tonal context of music. npj Science of Learning 8:22. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-023-00172-z

article_title: The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education.
citation: Almasi-Turk Sahar, Roozbehi Amrollah. (2026). The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09833-0
title: R-ISAM: a five-phase spiral framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education
description: R-ISAM is a five-phase spiral curriculum model integrating gross anatomy, histology, and embryology with radiology, surface anatomy, physical examination, and clinical reasoning. As the article states, "R-ISAM consists of five sequential phases that progressively integrate anatomical sciences with clinical reasoning, imaging interpretation, and procedural skills". The phases run from System Overview through Anatomical Radiology, Surface Anatomy, and System Examination to Integrated Clinical Anatomy, each building on the previous one. It is grounded in the spiral curriculum, Cognitive Load Theory, the ICAP framework, and alignment with CBME and Entrustable Professional Activities.
requirements: Sustained collaboration between basic science and clinical faculty, including joint planning meetings, workshops, and peer observation
Robust infrastructure: digital repositories, simulation facilities, small-group learning spaces, and online platforms for integrated content and assessments
Student support mechanisms including peer mentoring, formative feedback, and targeted academic assistance
constraints: Phases I and V are fixed, whereas Phases II, III, and IV can be rearranged or merged, expanded into four phases, or condensed into two
Phases I through IV can be planned and delivered within 8 to 10 weeks of a standard 16-week semester
target_learners: Undergraduate medical students in Basic Sciences through Clerkship stages
target_learning_goals: Clinical reasoning and physical examination skills
examples: Implemented across musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal systems between 2020 and 2025 in an undergraduate medical program, with more than 700 students exposed
key_sources: Almasi-Turk Sahar, Roozbehi Amrollah. (2026). The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09833-0

article_title: The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education.
citation: Almasi-Turk Sahar, Roozbehi Amrollah. (2026). The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09833-0
title: 65-item R-ISAM evaluation questionnaire with seven domains
description: A 65-item questionnaire developed to evaluate R-ISAM across seven domains (Basic Sciences Integration, Spiral Progression, Clinical Integration, Educational Environment, Teaching Methods, Assessment & Feedback, Overall Satisfaction). It was developed through item generation with an expert panel (n = 5 anatomy educators), content validity assessment using the Content Validity Index, pilot testing with 25 students, and reliability analysis. "The final instrument demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.989)" and factor analysis confirmed a seven-domain structure explaining 71.4% of variance.
requirements: Content validity assessment using the Content Validity Index and pilot testing before deployment
constraints: Developed and validated at a single institution with an anatomy-education focus
target_learners: Undergraduate medical students across Basic Sciences, Physiopathology, and Clerkship stages
target_learning_goals: Evaluation of perceived integration, teaching quality, assessment, and satisfaction in an integrated anatomy curriculum
examples: Administered simultaneously to all three stage groups during a single week with no examinations scheduled; response rate 27.5% (206 of 750 eligible students)
key_sources: Almasi-Turk Sahar, Roozbehi Amrollah. (2026). The Roozbehi Integrated Spiral Anatomy Model (R-ISAM): a five-phase framework for fully integrated anatomical sciences education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09833-0

article_title: Using R for data analysis and graphing in an introductory physics laboratory
citation: Primoˇz Peterlin. (2009). Using R for data analysis and graphing in an introductory physics laboratory. https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.4570
title: R language and computing environment for data manipulation, statistical computing, and scientific graphing
description: R is both a language and an environment for "data manipulation, statistical computing, and scienti ﬁc graphing", founded on the S language and distributed as free software via the Comprehensive R Archive Network. It uses a command-line interface, encourages vector-based programming, fits linear models with lm() and non-linear models with nls(), plots histograms with hist(), and exports graphs as PostScript, PDF, or bitmap files. Scripts can be saved and re-executed with source(), supporting reproducible workflows, and over 1500 contributed packages are available on CRAN.
requirements: Students cannot be expected to self-learn it; the article states a quick introduction course has been recommended even for graduate students
constraints: Students entering the laboratory course usually have no previous experience with R, and it lacks a point-and-click interface
target_learners: first-year university students of medicine, dental medicine and veterinary medicine in a physics laboratory course
target_learning_goals: data analysis and scientific graphing of laboratory measurements
examples: The paper scripts a bivariate regression of electrolyte conductivity on concentration, a two-exponential capacitor-discharge fit with nls(), and a radioactive-decay histogram with an overlaid normal density (x = 5.61, σx = 2.60).
key_sources: Primoˇz Peterlin. (2009). Using R for data analysis and graphing in an introductory physics laboratory. https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.4570

article_title: Meeting Student Needs for Multivariate Data Analysis: A Case Study in Teaching a Multivariate Data Analysis Course with No Pre-requisites
citation: Amy Wagaman, Amherst College. (2012). Meeting Student Needs for Multivariate Data Analysis: A Case Study in Teaching a Multivariate Data Analysis Course with No Pre-requisites. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Meeting+Student+Needs+for+Multivariate+Data+Analysis
title: R with RCommander (Rcmdr) plus Ggobi as course software for a no-prerequisite multivariate course
description: The course used R with the menu-driven RCommander graphical interface as primary software, chosen because students were not likely skilled programmers: "I decided to use R with R Commander (Rcmdr) as the primary software for the course". Rcmdr's menu-driven interface is a comfortable starting point and its script window exposes R syntax, and all students eventually had to use R script for some multivariate techniques. Ggobi was used to aid data visualization and exploration, interfacing with R via the Rggobi package. The author reports Rcmdr was sufficient for all techniques except MDS and classification.
requirements: First two weeks of computer lab devoted to learning the software and visualizing multivariate data
Lab activities designed with step-by-step instructions to avoid overwhelming students with software commands
constraints: Rcmdr was insufficient for MDS and classification, where raw R code or instructor-provided code and examples were used
target_learners: undergraduates assumed to be digital natives familiar with programs such as Excel but not skilled programmers
target_learning_goals: developing computational skills and performing multivariate analyses such as PCA, clustering, and classification
examples: Students performed PCA in Rcmdr via the Dimensional analysis submenu, obtaining scree plots, biplots, loadings, and percentages of variation explained
key_sources: Amy Wagaman, Amherst College. (2012). Meeting Student Needs for Multivariate Data Analysis: A Case Study in Teaching a Multivariate Data Analysis Course with No Pre-requisites. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Meeting+Student+Needs+for+Multivariate+Data+Analysis

article_title: Assessing the interactivity and prescriptiveness of faculty professional development workshops: The Real-Time Professional Development Observation Tool (R-PDOT)
citation: Alice Olmstead and Chandra Turpen. (2016). Assessing the interactivity and prescriptiveness of faculty professional development workshops: The Real-Time Professional Development Observation Tool (R-PDOT). arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07126v2
title: The Real-Time Professional Development Observation Tool (R-PDOT)
description: The R-PDOT is a descriptive, non-evaluative real-time observation instrument for faculty professional development workshops. Like COPUS, RIOT and TDOP, it "allows an observer to collect non-evaluative, quantitative data about what faculty participants experience during workshops," capturing two complementary dimensions simultaneously: type-of-engagement codes and focus-of-engagement codes. Each code set is intended to fully span the ways faculty are most likely to be engaged or to have their attention focused.
requirements: Trained observers applying shared codebooks; the article reports methods for refining codes, establishing inter-rater reliability, and visualizing data
constraints: The R-PDOT is not designed to characterize the nature of tasks, quality of written scaffolding, or exact in-the-moment facilitation moves
target_learners: STEM faculty participating in professional development workshops
target_learning_goals: Improving teaching through adoption and adaptation of research-based instructional strategies
examples: The authors analyze R-PDOT data from three sessions of the Physics and Astronomy New Faculty Workshop and use interviews with workshop leaders as preliminary evidence of its reflective utility
key_sources: Alice Olmstead and Chandra Turpen. (2016). Assessing the interactivity and prescriptiveness of faculty professional development workshops: The Real-Time Professional Development Observation Tool (R-PDOT). arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07126

article_title: Teachers' perception of Jupyter and R Shiny as digital tools for open education and science
citation: Jozef Hanˇc, Peter ˇStrauch, Eva Paˇnkov´a and Martina Hanˇcov´a. (2020). Teachers' perception of Jupyter and R Shiny as digital tools for open education and science. https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11262
title: Tailor-made R Shiny web application for teachers' educational data
description: A web application built by the authors with the R Shiny library to give in-service physics teachers access to their own educational data without adaptation learning. It "helps a teacher automatically collect his educational data from a Google form and transform it into interactive web presentation showing statistical analysis, graphical and numerical summaries with interpretation", via an intuitive point-and-click interface requiring no setup. Teachers collected data in June 2018 and explored it interactively in the app.
requirements: A Google form for data collection and the R Shiny library as the underlying web presentation technology
constraints: Designed for in-service teachers after a Jupyter pilot showed negative feedback, so it requires no setup and zero adaptation learning time
target_learning_goals: use of student preconception and misconception data to improve instruction
examples: Teachers collected physics-class data via an online Google form in school PC rooms and then interactively explored it in the R Shiny app before filling out an attitude questionnaire and UEQ
key_sources: Jozef Hanˇc, Peter ˇStrauch, Eva Paˇnkov´a and Martina Hanˇcov´a. (2020). Teachers' perception of Jupyter and R Shiny as digital tools for open education and science. https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11262

article_title: The Research Based Learning -- STEM Learning Activities: The Use of r-Dynamic Coloring to Improve the Students Metaliteracy in Solving a Tessellation Decoration Problem
citation: A I Kristiana, Dafik, Z R Ridlo, R M Prihandini, R Adawiyah. (2022). The Research Based Learning - STEM Learning Activities: The Use of r-Dynamic Coloring to Improve the Students Metaliteracy in Solving a Tessellation Decoration Problem. https://app.diagrams.net
title: r-Dynamic coloring of graphs as a technique for tessellation decoration
description: The article defines r-dynamic coloring: "By an r-dynamic coloring of a graph G, we mean a proper k-coloring of graph G such that the neighbors of any vertex v receive at least min{r, d(v)} different colors." The r-dynamic chromatic number is the minimum k for which such a coloring exists. The technique is applied to block paving tessellation decoration via a five-step procedure including drawing a dual graph, and the article instructs: "Please make sure that there does not exist two adjacent block paving sharing the same colors."
requirements: Graph representation of the tessellation as a dual graph, and determination of lower and upper bounds for the r-dynamic chromatic number
key_sources: A I Kristiana, Dafik, Z R Ridlo, R M Prihandini, R Adawiyah. (2022). The Research Based Learning - STEM Learning Activities: The Use of r-Dynamic Coloring to Improve the Students Metaliteracy in Solving a Tessellation Decoration Problem. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11673

article_title: Effects of the Tennessee Prekindergarten Program on children’s achievement and behavior through third grade
citation: Lipsey, M. W., Farran, D. C., & Durkin, K. (2018). Effects of the Tennessee Prekindergarten Program on children's achievement and behavior through third grade. Early Childhood Research Quarterly. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2018.03.005
title: R-List randomization procedure for oversubscribed pre-k programs
description: A randomization mechanism for evaluating a voluntary pre-k program when demand exceeds capacity. Oversubscribed programs submitted applicant lists, which the research team sorted into random order and returned; "program staff were asked to fill their pre-k seats in the order that children appeared on these randomized lists", with unoffered children becoming the waiting-list control group. Across two cohorts this generated 150 randomized applicant lists, of which 111 active R-Lists with 3,131 VPK-eligible children formed the study base.
requirements: Programs with more applicants than spaces, identified in advance via surveys of available seats and applications
Program staff compliance with the randomized admission order, with repeated contact attempts before moving to the next child
constraints: R-Lists were excluded when schools did not use the correct random order or when lists lacked children in both treatment and control conditions
target_learners: Low-income 4-year-old children applying to oversubscribed VPK programs
target_learning_goals: Estimating the causal effects of pre-k participation on achievement and behavior
examples: For the second cohort, staff were asked to attempt to contact a parent at least three times on different days before moving to the next child on the list
key_sources: Lipsey, M. W., Farran, D. C., & Durkin, K. (2018). Effects of the Tennessee Prekindergarten Program on children's achievement and behavior through third grade. Early Childhood Research Quarterly. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2018.03.005
